/consulting.h: Free tools for Level III and inspection planning
/consulting.p: Two planning tools and the templates behind most engagements, free and with nothing to sign up for.

/consulting/api-653-tank-inspector-servi.p: Screen your shell and floor intervals from your own thickness readings, then use the template to see what a complete API 653 record contains. The Authorized Inspector sets the final interval; the quotation names who performs each examination.

/consulting/api-510-pressure-vessel-insp.p: Work out the corrosion rate, remaining life and the maximum internal and external intervals from your own readings before the scope is written.

/consulting/api-570-piping-inspector-ser.p: Thickness intervals under API 570 depend on remaining life and piping class. Screen a circuit from your own readings first.
links: API 570 interval calculator by piping class

/inspection-services.h: Free planning tools for API 510, 570 and 653 work
/inspection-services.p: Screen intervals and remaining life from your own data, and see what a complete inspection record looks like before you send an RFQ.

/blog/api-653-tank-inspection-guide.h: Work out your own tank intervals
/blog/api-653-tank-inspection-guide.p: The interval rules in this guide are built into a free calculator: enter shell or floor readings and see the corrosion rate, remaining life and maximum interval.

/tools/corrosion-rate-calculator.h: Need the code interval, not a rule of thumb?
/tools/corrosion-rate-calculator.p: This calculator gives a corrosion rate and remaining life. For the maximum interval each inspection code allows — API 510 internal and external, API 570 by piping class, API 653 shell and floor — use the interval calculator, which compares long-term and short-term rates and applies the code limits.

/tools.p: Planning and field calculators added in October 2026. Each runs in your browser and sends nothing anywhere.

/resources/training-requirements-matrix.h: Turn the matrix into a plan
/resources/training-requirements-matrix.p: The hours planner uses the same figures as this matrix. Pick a method and level, enter what a technician has logged, and see what is left.

/resources/ndt-written-practice-template.p: Once the written practice sets the hours, track each technician against them.
links: Outsourced Level III: written practice authored and approved

/ndt-training-online.h: How many hours do you still need?
/ndt-training-online.p: Online theory covers the classroom hours; on-the-job experience is logged separately with your employer. The planner shows both against the recommended minimums.
links: How training, exams and certification fit together

/ndt-level-1-training.p: See the classroom and on-the-job hours for your method and how many you still need.

/ndt-level-2-training.p: Direct entry to Level 2 adds the Level 1 and Level 2 hours together. The planner does the arithmetic for your method.

/asnt-certification.p: Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you once training, experience and examinations are complete. Check where you stand on hours first.

/best-ndt-reporting-software-2026.p: Take the buyer checklist into every demo. It covers the enforcement, field, data and exit questions that feature lists leave out.

/ndt-inspection-software.p: A buyer checklist for NDT inspection software: certifications, calibration, field capture, approvals, data ownership and exit.

/erp.p: The buyer checklist lists what to make every vendor show you live, including where data is hosted, who can see it and how you get it back.

/digital-twin-reporting.p: Use the buyer checklist for the data, security and exit questions, and the interval calculator to check the remaining-life arithmetic yourself.
